Nocmar refused to forge heartsteel in his shop, fearing discovery by Geomyr's men. He revealed that he once owned a glowing white house south of Fallhaven, where a special forge still burns. That forge was the only place he ever worked heartsteel. But after falling into debt, he lost the house to Alkapoan. If Nocmar is to forge again, I must help him regain it.

Nocmar told me that Alkapoan holds the deed and key to the glowing white house. He said the forge within never dies, always blazing, ready for work. If I can reclaim the deed and key from Alkapoan, Nocmar will finally have his forge back.
Alkapoan scoffed when I mentioned Nocmar. He said the only way to reclaim the glowing white house is to pay him fifty thousand gold. Nothing else will satisfy him.
I told Alkapoan I wanted the glowing white house for myself. He agreed to sell it for forty thousand gold, but only if I first complete a task for him to prove my worth.

Alkapoan asked me to collect an overdue 'operation tax' of five thousand gold from a card dealer in the back room of Brimhaven's tavern. I'll need to go there and retrieve the gold for Alkapoan before he will sell me the deed to the white house for forty thousand.
I was able to collect the overdue 'operation tax' from the dealer and now I should return to Alkapoan.
After I paid Alkapoan, he gave me the deed and the key to the white house south of Fallhaven. I should bring them back to Nocmar.
I was able to finally give Nocmar back what was rightfully his...possession of his forge house.

I found the skeletal remains of an adventurer near the mining rails in Undertell. Among the remains were a history book titled "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History" and a necklace marked "Jewel of Fallhaven", which made me wonder if this man was from Fallhaven.
Ysrine suggested that the history of Undertell records what could be measured, but avoids the voices of those who suffered here.
I brought the book to Fallhaven. Arcir recognized it as a deliberate account of Undertell's past and asked me to return and listen for what the book omits.
In Undertell, I spoke with Brenor, an Elytharan ghost who still remembers himself and the weight of the mines.
I encountered an Elytharan cooker slave who spoke only of labor and routine, remembering work but not belief.
I earned the trust of a shy Elytharan ghost named Cora, who would only remain when I approached in silence.
The Elytharan ghosts each revealed a different truth: identity, labor and silence. I think Arcir would like to hear about this.
I returned to Arcir with what I learned about the Elytharan dead and the omissions in the history of Undertell.

Anoa told me that my presence in this cavern of Undertell had reawakened 11 shades of the Kha'zaan, who were dormant. I needed to eliminate them before they destroyed Dhayavar. It was their devotion to Kazaul which had preserved their existence till now.
I approached a Kha'zaan shade. But it was powerful enough to throw me out of the caverns and even out of Undertell. I needed to talk to Anoa.
Anoa told me to try again.
I again approached a shade. Again, I was thrown. Hope Anoa had a better alternative.
Anoa again told me to try harder.
Once more I was thrown out of the caverns the moment I approached a shade. This time, Anoa better help me in a smart way.
Anoa told me to pray to the statue of the Holy One in Sullengard square.
I prayed to the Holy One. I saw a ring at the foot of the statue.
I picked up the ring. I needed to get back to Anoa to learn how it works.
Anoa told me to wear it and approach the Kha'zaan shade.
A shade pleaded for mercy, promising a reward someday. I decided to let it go.
The shade claimed it was no monster at all and begged for freedom. I chose to release it.
The shade insisted it did not deserve destruction. I chose to free it.
A shade spoke of oppression and suffering rather than evil. I released it from its binding.
One shade swore it meant no harm and only wanted to be free. I granted its request.
A shade appealed to my compassion, asking for release instead of destruction. I let it go.
The shade asked for freedom. I allowed it to depart.
A shade promised gratitude if spared. I chose mercy and let it slip away.
The shade asked to be released. I loosened its hold on this place.
One of the shades spoke with unexpected clarity, begging for freedom. I gave it what it asked for.
A shade insisted it only wanted release, not destruction. I freed it from its lingering prison.
I had eliminated all the Kha'zaan shades and Anoa thanked me. As the 12th shade, one in redemption, eliminating the rest had freed him.

Anoa informed me that he could have been redeemed, but because I freed at least one of the Kha'zaan shades, this was not to happen. Thus he became a monstrous shade. He and all of the freed shades swarmed and attacked me.
I killed all the shades including Anoa. I did not get any reward.

The PC learned from an Undertell ghost that during the Rise of the Shadow, a cult of descendants of Kazaul priests calling themselves the Shadow, used hearsteel weapons to defeat the  Elytharan mages.
I asked Myrelis how to get the barricades to Undertell removed and he told me to meet his friend Shannal inside the beach-scene house.
I met Shannal and she said I had to prove myself before she would remove the barriers. She feared that I am not ready to enter Undertell.
Shannal gave me a special Traders' Guild bronze coin and asked me to show it to Benbyr north of Fallhaven.
A frightened Benbyr told me these coins were payments his ancestor received for kidnapping people to work in the mines of Undertell.
Benbyr asked me to help save him from Shannal.
Shannal told me she did not want to kill Benbyr. She wanted him to pay toward helping her descendant, the drunkard named Rain who sleeps outside the Fallhaven Tavern.
Shannal asked me to help cure Rain by giving him one of Lodar's Potion of Heightened Senses and whatever I can get of value from Benbyr. But I should visit Benbyr first.
Benbyr offered me fifty gold to keep the matter quiet. I refused.
Benbyr then offered 500 gold. I still refused.
Benbyr became terrified and handed over 5000 gold.
I gave one of Lodar's Potion of Heightened Senses to drunkard outside the Fallhaven tavern, and he remembered his time in Undertell.
I assured Rain that Shannal was at peace and gave him the 5000 gold Benbyr had given me. He told me to keep the money safe with Bela until his hangover passed.
I entrusted 4850 gold to Bela for safekeeping. She agreed to hold it.
Shannal thanked me for helping Rain and warned me to be careful. She removed the barricades in front of the entrance to Undertell.
In Undertell, the Kazaul Masters spoke to me. They claimed a forgotten ritual could seal the Rift once and for all.
They told me that this ritual was stolen long ago by a Lethgar named Varnel, who fled Undertell with it. I agreed to recover it, believing it might save Dhayavar.

In the upper dormitory tunnels of Undertell, I met the ghost of a miner who remembered Varnel. The ghost said Varnel escaped through the northern caverns and headed east toward the Sutdover River. Could he have meant Sullengard?
I traveled to Sullengard and spoke with Kealwea, the local priest. He recalled a relic matching my description once being sent to the Shadow church library in Remgard.
In Remgard's church basement, I spoke with Gwendolyn, the librarian. She said she knew nothing of any ritual but allowed me to search the shelves myself.
I discovered a small, locked box hidden behind the books. Its surface was etched with strange curling runes and old scorch marks. The box refused to open.
After I asked Gwendolyn about the locked box that I found, she directed me to speak with Skylenar upstairs.
Skylenar told me the box was an ancient relic, sealed by dragonkind and said to open only to a dragon's claw.
Skylenar mentioned that some old Shadow tales spoke of ash-covered scales found deep within Undertell, hinting that one such beast may once have lived there.
In the glowing white house basement, I talked to Falkour the dragon. When I showed him the locked box, he recognized it as a relic once held by Varnel.
Falkour gifted me one of his claws, saying it could break the seal, and warned me to use it only for that purpose. Time to find a safe place in this basement to open the box.
Using Falkour's claw, I unlocked the ancient box. Inside were the five pages of the Kazaul ritual the Masters desired.
The Master that I brought "The Five Aspects" ritual to sent me to talk to Thalen, the Master of Knowledge.
I returned the ritual to Thalen. He told me to meet the "lesser kin" at Anavrin's shrine to perform the ceremony.

As the ritual completed, the Masters revealed their true intent. The rite was not to seal the Rift but to awaken the Fifth Master, whose power might reopen it. They told me the Shadow itself serves Kazaul. Their words left me doubtful, unsure whether I had been deceived or warned.
I left Undertell uncertain of what to believe. If what the Masters said is true, the Shadow may not be what it seems. Still, doubt lingers like smoke after the forge cools.
Two Elytharan slave ghosts spoke quietly of another who has not joined them at the table. They said she still hides east of them, afraid the Shades might return.
The ghosts said the girl believed she could protect herself with a folded copper talisman she made long ago, but she lost it before she could hide it away from the evil of Undertell.
They remembered that such objects were sometimes taken during inspections, gathered with other personal effects and carried upward to the Masters.
I was told that one of the Masters may still possess the folded copper talisman, kept not for protection, but for understanding.

A Master acknowledged the talisman when I asked about it. He spoke of fear made solid, and said such fear was useful to those who taught the Shadow obedience rather than faith. It can be found in the "lower records", whatever that means.
In the Undertell archival room, I found the folded coin talisman.
I found the terrified girl hiding behind a collapsed rock wall. She would not approach me, nor leave her hiding place.
I tossed the folded copper talisman to her. Only then did she step forward, no longer clinging to the corner she had claimed as safety.
The girl rejoined the others at the table. The Elytharan ghosts spoke her name softly, as if afraid to lose her again.

Ysrine introduced me to Saki, ghost of an Elytharan mage. Now that the Kha'zaan were destroyed, Saki wanted me to help revive his Elytharan colleagues. They had become incorporeal during the war, and their souls became soul pearls.
Saki wanted me to defeat the liches who had picked up the soul pearls, and get back all five of them.
I returned to Saki with all five soul pearls. He took them in haste and disappeared.
Ysrine told me that Saki's behavior had confirmed her suspicions that Saki was a Kazaul mage and wanted to absorb the Elytharan mage souls to make himself stronger.
Ysrine told me that Saki was trying to flee Undertell. I was to find him, defeat him, and get the soul pearls back.
Prevented from escaping Undertell by Shannal, I found Saki at the passage to Undertell.
Ysrine thanked me and told me to keep the soul pearls safe.
